Surah 67 is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} {Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion} (تبارك): that is, He is magnified and exalted, His goodness is abundant and His kindness is all-encompassing. Among His greatness is that the dominion of the upper and lower worlds is in His hand; He is the One who created it and disposes of it as He wills, through the decrees of destiny and the religious laws that accord with His wisdom. And among His greatness is the perfection of His power, by which He is able to do all things, and by which He brought into existence the great creations that He brought into being, such as the heavens and the earth.

{2} And {He who created death and life}: that is, He decreed for His servants that He would give them life and then cause them to die; {that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed}: that is, the most sincere and the most correct in it. This is because Allah created His servants and brought them forth into this abode, informed them that they would be transferred from it, commanded and forbade them, and tested them with desires that oppose His command. Whoever submits to the command of Allah and does good deeds, Allah will reward him well in both abodes; and whoever inclines toward the desires of the self and casts aside the command of Allah, for him is the worst recompense. {And He is the Almighty}: the One to whom belongs all might, by which He has subdued all things and to whom all creatures are subservient. {The Forgiving}: toward those who do evil, those who fall short, and those who sin, especially when they repent and turn back in penitence; He forgives their sins, even if they reach the clouds of the sky, and He conceals their faults, even if they fill the earth.

{3} {He who created seven heavens in layers}: that is, each one above the other, not one single layer; and He created them in the utmost beauty and perfection. {You will not see in the creation of the Most Gracious any imperfection}: that is, no flaw or deficiency. When deficiency is absent in every respect, they become beautiful, complete and harmonious in every aspect, in their color, form, height, and what is in them of the sun [and the moon], the stars, the shining fixed stars and the wandering planets. Since their perfection is known, He, exalted is He, commanded repeated looking at them and contemplation of their expanses. He said: {Then look again [at the sky]}: that is, return your gaze to it, looking and reflecting; {do you see any rifts?}: that is, any deficiency or disorder.

{4} {Then look again, twice}: [and] what is meant by this is the frequency of repetition. {Your sight will return to you dulled, while it is exhausted}: that is, unable to see any flaw or rift, even if it strives to the utmost effort.

Then he explicitly mentioned its beauty, saying:

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 67, verses 5–11:**

{5} That is: And indeed We adorned {the nearest heaven} (al-sama' al-dunya), which you see and which is above you, {with lamps}, namely the stars, differing in their light and brightness. For were it not for the stars in it, it would be a dark ceiling with no beauty or elegance. But God made these stars an adornment for the heaven, a beauty, a light, and a guidance by which one is guided in the darknesses of land and sea. His statement that He adorned the nearest heaven with lamps does not preclude that many stars are beyond the seven heavens, for the heavens are transparent; thus the adornment of the nearest heaven is achieved even if the planets are not in it. {And We made them} – that is, the lamps – {missiles against the devils}, who seek to eavesdrop on news of the heavens. So God made these stars a guard for the heaven against the devils' snatching news of the earth. These shooting meteors that are hurled from the stars, God has prepared them in this world for the devils. {And We have prepared for them} – in the Hereafter – {the punishment of the Blaze}, because they rebelled against God and led His servants astray.

{6} For this reason, their followers among the disbelievers are like them, and God has prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze. Therefore He said: {And for those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination}, in which its people are humiliated to the utmost degree of humiliation.

{7} {When they are thrown into it}, in a manner of humiliation and abasement, {they will hear from it a roaring}, that is, a loud, dreadful sound.

{8} {It almost bursts with fury}; that is, it nearly splits apart from its own gathering and tears itself to pieces from the intensity of its rage against the disbelievers. So consider what it will do to them when they are gathered into it! Then He mentioned the rebuke of its keepers to its people, saying: {Every time a company is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them, "Did no warner come to you?"}; that is, your present state and your deserving of the Fire is as though you were never informed about it, nor were the warners to caution you against it.

{9} {They will say, "Yes, indeed, a warner came to us, but we denied and said, 'God has not sent down anything. You are only in great error.'"} So they combined their particular denial with a general denial of everything God sent down, and this did not suffice them, until they declared the misguidance of the warning messengers, who are the guides who are guided. They did not stop at mere error, but made their error a great error. What obstinacy, arrogance and wrongdoing resembles this?

{10} {And they will say}, acknowledging their unfitness for guidance and right conduct: {"If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze."} Thus they negated from themselves the paths of guidance: hearing what God sent down and the messengers brought, and the reason that benefits its possessor, leads him to the realities of things, prefers good, and restrains him from whatever has a blameworthy outcome. So they have neither hearing nor reason. This is in contrast with the people of certainty and knowledge, and the masters of truthfulness and faith, for they supported their faith with textual evidence, so they heard what came from God and what the Messenger of God brought, as knowledge, recognition and action, along with rational proofs that distinguish guidance from error, the good from the bad, and the beneficial from the harmful. Their faith is in proportion to what God has bestowed upon them of following both reason and transmitted texts. Glory be to Him who singles out whom He wills with His grace, bestows favor on whom He wills of His servants, and forsakes those unfit for good.

{11} God said, concerning these who enter the Fire and acknowledge their wrongdoing and obstinacy: {So they will acknowledge their sin. Then away with the companions of the Blaze!}; that is, distance, loss and misery for them. How wretched and ruined they are, since they missed God's reward and were bound to the Blaze that blazes in their bodies and rises over their hearts.

His statement that He adorned the nearest heaven with lamps does not preclude that many stars are beyond the seven heavens, for the heavens are transparent; thus the adornment of the nearest heaven is achieved even if the planets are not in it. {And We made them} – that is, the lamps – {missiles against the devils}, who seek to eavesdrop on news of the heavens. So God made these stars a guard for the heaven against the devils' snatching news of the earth. These shooting meteors that are hurled from the stars, God has prepared them in this world for the devils. {And We have prepared for them} – in the Hereafter – {the punishment of the Blaze}, because they rebelled against God and led His servants astray.

{6} For this reason, their followers among the disbelievers are like them, and God has prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze. Therefore He said: {And for those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination}, in which its people are humiliated to the utmost degree of humiliation.

{7} {When they are thrown into it}, in a manner of humiliation and abasement, {they will hear from it a roaring}, that is, a loud, dreadful sound.

{8} {It almost bursts with fury}; that is, it nearly splits apart from its own gathering and tears itself to pieces from the intensity of its rage against the disbelievers. So consider what it will do to them when they are gathered into it! Then He mentioned the rebuke of its keepers to its people, saying: {Every time a company is thrown into it, its keepers will ask them, "Did no warner come to you?"}; that is, your present state and your deserving of the Fire is as though you were never informed about it, nor were the warners to caution you against it.

{9} {They will say, "Yes, indeed, a warner came to us, but we denied and said, 'God has not sent down anything. You are only in great error.'"} So they combined their particular denial with a general denial of everything God sent down, and this did not suffice them, until they declared the misguidance of the warning messengers, who are the guides who are guided. They did not stop at mere error, but made their error a great error. What obstinacy, arrogance and wrongdoing resembles this?

{10} {And they will say}, acknowledging their unfitness for guidance and right conduct: {"If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not have been among the companions of the Blaze."} Thus they negated from themselves the paths of guidance: hearing what God sent down and the messengers brought, and the reason that benefits its possessor, leads him to the realities of things, prefers good, and restrains him from whatever has a blameworthy outcome. So they have neither hearing nor reason. This is in contrast with the people of certainty and knowledge, and the masters of truthfulness and faith, for they supported their faith with textual evidence, so they heard what came from God and what the Messenger of God brought, as knowledge, recognition and action, along with rational proofs that distinguish guidance from error, the good from the bad, and the beneficial from the harmful. Their faith is in proportion to what God has bestowed upon them of following both reason and transmitted texts. Glory be to Him who singles out whom He wills with His grace, bestows favor on whom He wills of His servants, and forsakes those unfit for good.

{11} God said, concerning these who enter the Fire and acknowledge their wrongdoing and obstinacy: {So they will acknowledge their sin. Then away with the companions of the Blaze!}; that is, distance, loss and misery for them. How wretched and ruined they are, since they missed God's reward and were bound to the Blaze that blazes in their bodies and rises over their hearts.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 67, verse 12:

{12} When He mentioned the state of the wretched sinners, He mentioned the description of the righteous, the happy ones, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen﴾; that is, in all their circumstances, even in the state in which none sees them except Allah. So they do not commit His disobediences, nor do they fall short of what He has commanded them. ﴿For them is forgiveness﴾: for their sins. And when Allah forgives their sins, He protects them from their evil and protects them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire. ﴿And for them is a great reward﴾: which is what Allah has prepared for them in Paradise of lasting bliss, great dominion, continuous pleasures, palaces, lofty dwellings, beautiful companions (hur), servants and youths (wildan). And greater and more magnificent than all of that is the good pleasure of the Most Merciful, which He bestows upon the dwellers of the Gardens.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 67, verses 13–14:

{13} This is an informing from God of the vastness of His knowledge and the comprehensiveness of His gentleness. He said: ﴿And keep your speech secret or declare it openly﴾; that is, all of it is equal to Him, and nothing hidden in it is concealed from Him. ﴿Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾; that is, of the intentions and volitions contained within them. So how much more of the statements and actions that are heard and seen?!

{14} Then He said, adducing a rational proof of His knowledge: ﴿Should not He who created know?﴾ For whoever created creatures, perfected them, and made them good, how could He not know them?! ﴿And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted﴾: whose knowledge and awareness are so subtle that they reach the innermost secrets, the consciences, the hidden things, the concealed things, and the unseen. ﴿And He knows what is secret and what is more hidden﴾. Among the meanings of "al-Latif" (the Subtle) is that He is the One who is gentle (yalutfu) with His servant and friend, bringing to him goodness and kindness from where he does not perceive, protecting him from evil from where he does not expect, and elevating him to the highest ranks by means that never occur to the servant's mind, to the extent that He makes him taste hardships in order to bring him through them to noble loves and lofty aims.

{15} That is, it is He who subjected the earth to you and made it submissive, so that you may obtain from it everything your needs depend upon: planting, building, tilling, and roads by which you can reach distant regions and far-off lands. {So walk in its broad tracts}; that is, to seek provision and gains. {And eat of His provision, and to Him is the resurrection}; that is, after you move on from this abode, which God made a trial and a provision by which one is sustained toward the Hereafter; you will be raised after your death and gathered to God, so that He may recompense you for your good and evil deeds.

This is a warning and threat to whoever persists in his transgression, his overstepping, and his disobedience, which necessitates punishment and the descent of retribution. So He says: {Are you secure from He who is in the heaven}, meaning Allah, the Exalted above His creation, {that He will not cause the earth to swallow you, and suddenly it shakes?}: with you, and it convulses until you perish and are destroyed.

{17–18} {Or are you secure from He who is in the heaven that He will not send upon you a storm of stones?}; i.e., a punishment from the sky that pelts you, and Allah takes vengeance upon you. {And you will know how My warning was}; i.e., how there will come to you what the messengers and the books warned you of. So do not suppose that your security from Allah, that He will not punish you with a punishment from the earth or from the sky, will benefit you. You will find the outcome of your affair, whether the term is long for you or short, for those before you denied as you have denied, and Allah destroyed them. So look at how Allah's denunciation of them was: He hastened to them the worldly punishment before the punishment of the Hereafter. So beware lest there befall you what befell them.

This is a rebuke and an exhortation to reflect on the state of the birds, which God subjected and for which He subjected the air and atmosphere: they spread their wings for flight and fold them for landing, so they remain floating in the air, moving about in it according to their will and need. {Nothing holds them up except the All-Merciful}: for He is the One who subjected the air to them and made their bodies and created form in a state prepared for flight. Whoever looks at the state of the bird and reflects upon it is guided by it to the power of the Creator and His divine providence, and that He is the One, the Unique, the only one worthy of worship. {Indeed He is All-Seeing of everything}: He is the one who manages His servants in what befits them and what His wisdom requires.

{20} Almighty God says to the obstinate ones who turn away from His command and refuse the truth: ﴿Or who is this that could be a host for you to help you, other than the Most Merciful?﴾ That is: who will help you if the Most Merciful intends harm for you and so repels it from you? In other words, who will help you against your enemies other than the Most Merciful? For He, exalted is He, is the Helper, the Mighty, the One who humbles whomever He wills. As for other creatures, even if they all gathered together to help a servant, they would not benefit him in the least, against any enemy whatsoever. Thus, the persistence of the disbelievers in their disbelief, after they have come to know that no one can help them other than the Most Merciful, is delusion and foolishness.

{21} ﴿Or who is this that could provide for you if He withheld His provision?﴾ That is: all provision comes from God. So if He withheld provision from you, who would send it to you? For creatures cannot provide for themselves, so how could they provide for others? Thus the Provider, the Bestower of blessings, from whom no blessing reaches the servants except by Him, is the One who deserves to be singled out for worship. But the disbelievers ﴿persisted﴾ (lajju); that is, they continued ﴿in arrogance﴾ (utuw); that is, in hardness and unwillingness to yield to the truth, ﴿and aversion﴾ (nufur); that is, fleeing from the truth.

{22} That is: which of the two men is better guided? The one who is wandering lost in misguidance, submerged in disbelief, whose heart has been overturned so that truth becomes falsehood to him and falsehood truth? Or the one who knows the truth, prefers it, acts upon it, and walks upon the straight path in his words, his deeds, and all his circumstances? By merely looking at the condition of the two men, one knows the difference between them, and which of them is guided and which is astray. Conditions are the greatest witness over statements.

{23} Almighty God says, making clear that He alone is the one to be worshipped, and calling His servants to thank Him and to worship Him alone: {He it is who brought you into being}; that is, He brought you into existence from nothing, without any helper or assistant. And when He brought you into being, He completed your existence for you with hearing, sight and hearts (af'idah). These three are the most excellent of the body's organs and the most complete of the bodily faculties. Yet despite this blessing, {little is it that you give thanks}: few among you are thankful, and few is the thanks you give.

{24} {Say: "It is He who multiplied you upon the earth"}; that is, He scattered you throughout its regions and settled you in its corners, commanded and forbade you, and bestowed upon you blessings by which you benefit. Then, after that, He will gather you for the Day of Resurrection. But these obstinate deniers reject this promise of recompense.

{25} {And they say}, in denial: {"When will this promise be, if you are truthful?"} They made the sign of their truthfulness to be that they be informed of the time of its coming. This is injustice and obstinacy.

{26} {Knowledge of it is only with God}: not with anyone among creation. And there is no necessary connection between this report and the information about its time, for truthfulness is known by its proofs. God has established, among the proofs and demonstrations of its truth, what leaves no slightest doubt for whoever gives ear while being a witness.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 67, verses 27–30:

{27} This means that the place of the disbelievers' denial and their delusion about it was while they were in this world. When the Day of Recompense comes, and they see the punishment near them, {zulfah} (nearby), it will distress them, horrify them and disturb them, so their faces will change because of it. They will be rebuked for their denial, and it will be said to them: {This is what you used to call for.} Today you have seen it with your own eyes, the matter has become clear to you, your means have been cut off, and nothing remains but direct contact with the punishment.

{28} Since those who denied the Messenger (ﷺ) and who turned away from his call were waiting for his destruction and watching for the calamities of fate to befall him, Allah commanded him to say to them: Even if your wish is fulfilled and {Allah destroys me and those with me}, that will not benefit you in the least, because you have disbelieved in the signs of Allah and deserved the punishment. So who will protect you {from a painful punishment}? It has been decreed that it will certainly befall you. Therefore your toil and your eagerness for my destruction will be of no use or benefit to you whatsoever.

{29} Among their claims was that they are upon guidance while the Messenger is in error. They repeated and expanded upon this, argued for it and fought over it. So Allah commanded His Prophet to inform them about his own state and the state of his followers, by which the guidance and piety of each person becomes clear, namely that they should say: {We have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied.} Faith (iman) encompasses inward assent, inward deeds and outward deeds. Since the existence and perfection of deeds depend upon reliance (tawakkul), Allah singled out tawakkul from among all the other deeds, though it is included in faith and is one of its necessary components, as He, the Exalted, said: {And upon Allah rely, if you are believers.} So when this is the state of the Messenger and of those who follow him, and it is the state that is required for success and upon which happiness depends, while the state of his enemies is its opposite, then they have no faith and no reliance. Thereby it becomes known who is upon guidance and who is in clear error.

{30} Then He informed of His sole possession of blessings, especially water, from which Allah made every living thing, saying: {Say: Have you considered, if your water should sink away} (ghawran), meaning sinking into the earth, {then who will bring you flowing water?} You drink from it, water your livestock, your trees and your crops. This is a question carrying the meaning of negation: no one can do that except Allah, the Exalted.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Mulk, and praise be to Allah.

So who will protect you {from a painful punishment}? It has been decreed that it will certainly befall you. Therefore your toil and your eagerness for my destruction will be of no use or benefit to you whatsoever.

{29} Among their claims was that they are upon guidance while the Messenger is in error. They repeated and expanded upon this, argued for it and fought over it. So Allah commanded His Prophet to inform them about his own state and the state of his followers, by which the guidance and piety of each person becomes clear, namely that they should say: {We have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied.} Faith (iman) encompasses inward assent, inward deeds and outward deeds. Thereby it becomes known who is upon guidance and who is in clear error.

This is a question carrying the meaning of negation: no one can do that except Allah, the Exalted.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Mulk, and praise be to Allah.
